review.automatedChecks: tests/explanations.test.ts: sentences of at most twenty-five words, no digits, every technical term declared and defined in the glossary, a 'what to do' in every problem, real axe-core and Lighthouse ids, the same entries as the Portuguese catalog.
review.humanReview: Missing: a reading of the text by a person. Record here who reviewed it and when.

glossary.HTML: The code that builds the page's content, such as text, images and links.
glossary.CSS: The code that sets the page's look, such as colors, sizes and positions.
glossary.JavaScript: The code that makes the page react to clicks and change without reloading.
glossary.attribute: An extra piece of information written inside a piece of markup in the page's code.
glossary.alt: The alternative text of an image. It describes the image to people who cannot see it.
glossary.contrast: The difference in brightness between the text and the background behind it.
glossary.screen reader: A program that reads the page aloud for people who are blind or have low vision.
glossary.browser: The program used to open sites, such as Chrome, Safari or Firefox.
glossary.server: The computer that stores the site and sends it to whoever visits.
glossary.cache: A copy the browser keeps so it does not download the same file again.
glossary.compression: A way to shrink text files before sending them, without losing any of the content.
glossary.KB: Kilobyte, the unit used to measure file size. The larger the number, the longer the download takes.
glossary.ARIA: A set of extra markup that explains parts of the page to screen readers.
glossary.focus: The mark that shows where the keyboard is on the page, when moving with the Tab key.
glossary.WebP: A modern image format, which takes less space at the same quality.
glossary.AVIF: Another modern image format, which usually takes even less space than WebP.
glossary.3G: An old and slow kind of mobile internet connection.
glossary.JSON: A data file made for programs to read. The numbers in this report come from it.
glossary.Lighthouse: A free tool from Google that measures the speed of web pages.
glossary.axe: A free tool that looks for accessibility barriers in web pages.
glossary.accessibility: How far the page can be used by everyone, including people with disabilities.
glossary.WCAG: The international accessibility guidelines for the web. This check uses levels A and AA.
glossary.kbit/s: Kilobits per second, the measure of internet speed. The smaller the number, the slower the connection.

report.title: Site report
report.intro: This report shows how much the page weighs and how long it takes to appear on a phone with a weak connection. It also shows what stops some people from using it.
report.introSources: The numbers come from two tools, Lighthouse and axe, and are in the JSON files saved beside this report.
report.introTerms: The technical words are explained at the end, in the section of words used.
report.weightIntro: Each visit downloads these files. On a phone, each file costs time and part of the data plan.
report.loadHeading: Time to appear on a phone with 3G
report.loadIntro: Lighthouse simulates an ordinary phone on a 3G connection and measures how long each part of the page takes to appear.
report.loadProfile: Simulated connection: a round-trip wait of {rtt} milliseconds, a speed of {kbps} kbit/s and a processor {cpu} times slower than the measuring computer.
report.speedHeading: What makes the page heavy or slow
report.speedNone: Lighthouse found no weight or speed problem on this page.
report.speedGainLcp: Fixing this can make the main part appear up to {seconds} seconds sooner.
report.speedGainFcp: Fixing this can make the first thing appear up to {seconds} seconds sooner.
report.a11yIntro: The axe tool looked for barriers that the WCAG guidelines ask to remove. Each one stops or hinders someone from using the page.
report.a11yNone: The axe tool found no barrier under the WCAG rules on this page.
report.a11yNote: Automatic tools find only part of the barriers. A test with real people is still needed.
report.a11yPlaces: It appears in {places} places on the page.
report.a11yPlacesOne: It appears in one place on the page.
report.a11yMore: More places are in the axe file.
report.noExplanationNote: This problem has no plain-language explanation yet. Below is the tool's original text.
report.sourcesIntro: Each number above can be checked in the JSON files in this folder, at the place shown below.
report.sourcesWeight: Weight by type: sum of the files of the same type, in the Lighthouse file
report.sourcesTotal: Total downloaded: sum of all files, equal to Lighthouse's own total
report.sourcesTime: Times: measured value of each metric, in milliseconds, in the Lighthouse file
report.sourcesProfile: Simulated connection: settings used by Lighthouse
report.sourcesGain: Possible gains: estimated saving of each problem, in milliseconds, in the Lighthouse file
report.sourcesA11y: Barriers and places: the axe list of barriers and the places of each one

first-contentful-paint.title: First thing on the screen
first-contentful-paint.what: How long until the first text or image appears. Before that, the person sees a blank screen.

largest-contentful-paint.title: Main part on the screen
largest-contentful-paint.what: How long until the largest text or image on the screen appears. That is when the page looks ready to the visitor.

total-byte-weight.title: The page is heavy
total-byte-weight.what: The whole page is heavy to download. On a phone with a weak connection, this delays everything and uses up the data plan.
total-byte-weight.fix: Start with the largest files in the weight table. Images are usually the first to shrink.

image-delivery-insight.title: Images larger than they need to be
image-delivery-insight.what: Some images have more detail or more weight than the size they are shown at on the screen.
image-delivery-insight.fix: Save each image at the size it is shown at and use a modern format, such as WebP or AVIF.

render-blocking-insight.title: Files that hold the page blank
render-blocking-insight.what: The browser waits for some look or code files to finish downloading before showing anything.
render-blocking-insight.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to load these files later, or to put the essentials inside the page itself.

lcp-discovery-insight.title: The main image has no priority
lcp-discovery-insight.what: The browser does not know the main image is the most important one and does not download it first.
lcp-discovery-insight.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to mark the main image as a priority and never delay its loading.

network-dependency-tree-insight.title: Files that wait for others
network-dependency-tree-insight.what: Some files only start downloading after another one finishes. On a slow connection, each wait adds time.
network-dependency-tree-insight.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to shorten these waits and tell the browser early about the important files.

cache-insight.title: Files downloaded again on every visit
cache-insight.what: The server does not let the browser keep the files. Whoever comes back to the site downloads everything again.
cache-insight.fix: Set the server to allow a long cache for images and files that change little.

document-latency-insight.title: The page is slow to start arriving
document-latency-insight.what: The server is slow to answer, sends the visitor to another address first or sends the text without compression.
document-latency-insight.fix: Check the hosting, avoid needless address detours and turn on compression on the server.

font-display-insight.title: Text invisible while the font arrives
font-display-insight.what: The text stays hidden until the site's own font finishes downloading.
font-display-insight.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to show the text in a common font while the site's own font arrives.

unused-css-rules.title: Look rules the page does not use
unused-css-rules.what: The page downloads CSS rules it does not use. They add weight and bring nothing to the visitor.
unused-css-rules.fix: Remove the rules no page uses, or separate the rules of each page.

unused-javascript.title: Interactive code the page does not use
unused-javascript.what: The page downloads JavaScript code that does not run on it.
unused-javascript.fix: Remove code packages and parts that are not used, or load each part only where it is needed.

unminified-css.title: Look files with spare spaces
unminified-css.what: The CSS file goes out with spaces, line breaks and comments that only help whoever writes the code.
unminified-css.fix: Turn on the option to shrink files in your site-building tool or in your hosting before publishing.

unminified-javascript.title: Interactive code with spare spaces
unminified-javascript.what: The JavaScript file goes out with spaces, line breaks and comments that only help whoever writes the code.
unminified-javascript.fix: Turn on the option to shrink files in your site-building tool or in your hosting before publishing.

legacy-javascript-insight.title: Extra code for old browsers
legacy-javascript-insight.what: The page sends extra code to work in old browsers. Current browsers do not need it.
legacy-javascript-insight.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to produce the code only for current browsers.

duplicated-javascript-insight.title: Repeated code
duplicated-javascript-insight.what: The same code package appears more than once, and the phone downloads every copy.
duplicated-javascript-insight.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to keep a single copy of each code package.

third-parties-insight.title: Other companies' services weighing on the page
third-parties-insight.what: Tools from other companies, such as chats, ads and visit counters, download files and keep the phone busy.
third-parties-insight.fix: Keep only the services you really use and remove the others.

unsized-images.title: Images without a set size
unsized-images.what: Some images do not state their width and height. The content jumps around when they finish arriving.
unsized-images.fix: State the width and height of each image in the page's code.

dom-size-insight.title: Page with too many parts
dom-size-insight.what: The page has a very large number of blocks. The phone is slow to build and update everything.
dom-size-insight.fix: Split long content into more pages and remove hidden blocks nobody uses.

bootup-time.title: Interactive code slow to run
bootup-time.what: The phone spends a lot of time processing the page's JavaScript code.
bootup-time.fix: Remove code and services that are not essential, or load them after the page appears.

mainthread-work-breakdown.title: The phone works too hard to build the page
mainthread-work-breakdown.what: The phone's processor stays busy for a long time with the page's look, code and drawing.
mainthread-work-breakdown.fix: Reduce interactive code and heavy visual effects, starting with the ones you do not use.

viewport-insight.title: Page not fitted to the phone screen
viewport-insight.what: The page does not tell the phone it should fit the screen width, and touch can be slow to respond.
viewport-insight.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to add, at the start of the page, the markup that fits it to the phone screen.

modern-http-insight.title: Files delivered the old way
modern-http-insight.what: The server delivers the files with an old version of the web's rules, slower when there are many files.
modern-http-insight.fix: Ask the hosting to turn on the current version of file delivery.

color-contrast.title: Text hard to read
color-contrast.what: The text has little contrast with the background. People with low vision, or reading in the sun, cannot read it.
color-contrast.fix: Darken the text or lighten the background until reading is easy. A contrast tool shows when it passes.

image-alt.title: Image without a description
image-alt.what: The image has no alternative text, the alt. Someone using a screen reader does not know what it shows.
image-alt.fix: Write in the alt what the image shows, in a few words. If it is only decoration, leave the alt empty.

label.title: Form field without a name
label.what: A form field has no name tied to it. Someone using a screen reader does not know what to fill in.
label.fix: Put visible text beside each field and tie that text to the field in the code.

link-name.title: Link without text
link-name.what: A link has no text saying where it leads. Often it is an icon on its own.
link-name.fix: Write text in the link, or give the icon a name the screen reader can read.

button-name.title: Button without a name
button-name.what: A button has no text saying what it does. Someone using a screen reader hears only the word button.
button-name.fix: Write text in the button, or give the button's icon a name the screen reader can read.

input-button-name.title: Form button without a name
input-button-name.what: A form button has no text saying what it does.
input-button-name.fix: Write on the button what it does, such as send or search.

input-image-alt.title: Image button without a description
input-image-alt.what: A button made with an image has no alternative text. Someone using a screen reader does not know what it does.
input-image-alt.fix: Write in the image's alt what the button does, such as send or search.

html-has-lang.title: Page without a stated language
html-has-lang.what: The page does not say what language it is written in. The screen reader may read the text with the wrong accent.
html-has-lang.fix: State the page's language in the code, for example American English.

html-lang-valid.title: Page language written wrong
html-lang-valid.what: The language stated in the page's code does not exist in the official list of languages.
html-lang-valid.fix: Correct the language code. For American English, use that language's official code.

valid-lang.title: Language of a passage written wrong
valid-lang.what: A passage of the page states a language that does not exist in the official list of languages.
valid-lang.fix: Correct that passage's language code, or delete the information if the passage is in the page's language.

document-title.title: Page without a title
document-title.what: The page has no title. The title is what shows in the browser tab and what the screen reader reads first.
document-title.fix: Give the page a short title that says the site's name and the page's subject.

select-name.title: List of options without a name
select-name.what: A choice list has no name. Someone using a screen reader does not know what they are choosing.
select-name.fix: Put visible text beside the list and tie that text to the list in the code.

frame-title.title: Embedded content without a name
frame-title.what: Content from another site inside the page, such as a map or video, has no name.
frame-title.fix: Give that content a short name that says what it is, such as store map.

meta-viewport.title: Page blocks zoom
meta-viewport.what: The page does not let the person enlarge the text with their fingers. People who see little need the zoom.
meta-viewport.fix: Remove from the page's code the rule that blocks zoom.

meta-refresh.title: Page that reloads by itself
meta-refresh.what: The page reloads or changes address by itself after a while. The person loses what they were reading.
meta-refresh.fix: Remove the automatic reload, or let the person choose when to update.

list.title: List built the wrong way
list.what: A list has, inside it, parts that are not items. The screen reader counts the items wrong.
list.fix: Leave only the list's items inside it, and put the rest outside.

listitem.title: List item outside a list
listitem.what: A list item is loose, outside a list. The screen reader does not announce it as part of a list.
listitem.fix: Put the item inside a list, or turn it into ordinary text.

role-img-alt.title: Figure without a description
role-img-alt.what: An element marked as an image has no description. Someone using a screen reader does not know what it shows.
role-img-alt.fix: Give that image a short name that says what it shows.

svg-img-alt.title: Drawing without a description
svg-img-alt.what: A drawing or icon marked as an image has no description for someone using a screen reader.
svg-img-alt.fix: Give the drawing a short name that says what it shows.

aria-required-attr.title: Incomplete accessibility markup
aria-required-attr.what: A part of the page uses ARIA markup, but a piece of information it requires is missing.
aria-required-attr.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to complete that part's ARIA markup, or remove it.

aria-valid-attr-value.title: Accessibility markup with a wrong value
aria-valid-attr-value.what: A piece of ARIA markup has a value that does not exist. The screen reader may announce something false.
aria-valid-attr-value.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to correct the value of that part's ARIA markup.

aria-valid-attr.title: Accessibility markup with a wrong name
aria-valid-attr.what: A piece of ARIA markup has a name that does not exist, and the screen reader ignores it.
aria-valid-attr.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to correct the name of that part's ARIA markup.

aria-allowed-attr.title: Accessibility markup in the wrong place
aria-allowed-attr.what: A piece of ARIA markup was used on a part of the page that does not accept it.
aria-allowed-attr.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to remove that ARIA markup or swap it for an allowed one.

aria-hidden-focus.title: Hidden part the keyboard reaches
aria-hidden-focus.what: A part is hidden from the screen reader, but the keyboard still reaches it. The person cannot tell where they are.
aria-hidden-focus.fix: Take that part out of the keyboard's path, or let the screen reader see it.

aria-command-name.title: Command without a name
aria-command-name.what: A button or link made with ARIA markup has no name. Someone using a screen reader does not know what it does.
aria-command-name.fix: Give that command a short name that says what it does.

aria-input-field-name.title: Field without a name
aria-input-field-name.what: A field made with ARIA markup has no name. Someone using a screen reader does not know what to fill in.
aria-input-field-name.fix: Give that field a visible name that says what to fill in.

nested-interactive.title: Button inside a button
nested-interactive.what: A clickable control is inside another one. The keyboard and the screen reader cannot reach the inner one.
nested-interactive.fix: Separate the two controls, one beside the other.

link-in-text-block.title: Link told apart only by color
link-in-text-block.what: A link in the middle of text differs only by its color. People who cannot tell colors apart do not find it.
link-in-text-block.fix: Underline the links that sit in the middle of text.

autocomplete-valid.title: Autofill set up wrong
autocomplete-valid.what: A field asks for a kind of autofill that does not exist. The browser cannot help fill it in.
autocomplete-valid.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to use one of the official kinds of autofill, such as name or email.

video-caption.title: Video without captions
video-caption.what: A video has no captions. People who are deaf or have the sound off do not understand what is said.
video-caption.fix: Add captions to the video with what is said and the important sounds.

object-alt.title: Embedded content without a description
object-alt.what: A piece of content embedded in the page has no alternative text for someone using a screen reader.
object-alt.fix: Give that content a text that says what it shows.

area-alt.title: Clickable image area without a description
area-alt.what: A clickable part of an image has no alternative text. Someone using a screen reader does not know where it leads.
area-alt.fix: Write in each area's alt where it leads.

bypass.title: No shortcut to the content
bypass.what: There is no way to skip the menu and go straight to the content. Keyboard users pass through the whole menu on every page.
bypass.fix: Add a link to skip to the content at the start of the page, or mark the main regions in the code.

form-field-multiple-labels.title: Field with more than one name
form-field-multiple-labels.what: A form field has two or more names tied to it. The screen reader may read the wrong name.
form-field-multiple-labels.fix: Leave a single name tied to each field.

scrollable-region-focusable.title: Scrolling area the keyboard cannot reach
scrollable-region-focusable.what: An area of the page scrolls, but someone using only the keyboard cannot get to it to scroll.
scrollable-region-focusable.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to make that area reachable by keyboard.

duplicate-id-aria.title: Repeated internal names
duplicate-id-aria.what: Two parts of the page use the same internal name, and the screen reader ties the description to the wrong part.
duplicate-id-aria.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to give each part a unique internal name.

aria-roles.title: Markup for a kind of part that does not exist
aria-roles.what: A part of the page claims to be something using ARIA markup that does not exist.
aria-roles.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to correct or remove that ARIA markup.

aria-required-children.title: Group without the parts it should have
aria-required-children.what: A part marked with ARIA as a group, list or menu does not contain the items that kind requires.
aria-required-children.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to complete the group's items or correct the ARIA markup.

aria-required-parent.title: Item outside the right group
aria-required-parent.what: An item marked with ARIA, such as a menu item, is outside the group it belongs to.
aria-required-parent.fix: Ask whoever looks after the site to put the item inside the right group.
